caption: Sine: the raw sine, -1..1, remapped into 0..1 for brightness - smooth bands rolling across
why: The sine is the shape of every smooth swing: a pendulum, a wave, a breath. Sine gives it raw: -1..1, one full wave for each turn of its input - the building block the other wave nodes are made from.

Because it goes negative, it needs remapping before it lights anything. Its neighbours: Cosine gives a 0..1 hump directly; Wave gives 0..1 with cycles and other shapes; Math has sin, cos and tan in turns; Sine is the raw function.
steps: **Coords** `u` times 2 (a **Multiply**) plus a clock (**Time** times 0.3, an **Add**) is the **x** input: two turns across the matrix.
Sine of it swings from -1 to 1 and back twice across.
A **Remap** (in low -1, in high 1, out low 0, out high 1) moves that into 0..1 for the **Palette**'s brightness.
The trace shows the raw sine at the centre pixel - going below 0, which is why the Remap is there.

try.label: Only the top half
try.text: the Remap's in low at 0: the negative half all maps below 0 and goes dark - only the tops of the waves show, with long gaps.

try.label: More waves
try.text: the Multiply at 5: five waves across.
